title: Rigveda 6.43: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.43: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.43 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 449v-450r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.43.1 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 7, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 449v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>yasya̱ tyac chamba̍ra̱m made̱ divo̍dāsāya ra̱ndhaya̍ḥ | a̱yaṁ sa soma̍ indra te su̱taḥ piba̍ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>IN whose wild joy thou madest once Ṣambara Divodâsa's prey, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 449v (numbered 122v by the scribe) (OPenn image 450, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.42.1 ‹-apaścāt-daghvane nare›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 450r (numbered 123r by the scribe), begins in RV 6.43.2 ‹yasya tīvra-sutam madam madhyam›. Verse 6.43.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>yasya | tyat | śambaram | made | divaḥ-dāsāya | randhayaḥ | ayam | saḥ | somaḥ | indra | te | sutaḥ | piba

translation.original_ref: RV 6.43.2-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 7, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 450r
translation.original_text:
2yasya̍ tīvra̱suta̱m mada̱m madhya̱m anta̍ṁ ca̱ rakṣa̍se | a̱yaṁ sa soma̍ indra te su̱taḥ piba̍ ||
3yasya̱ gā a̱ntar aśma̍no̱ made̍ dṛ̱ḻhā a̱vāsṛ̍jaḥ | a̱yaṁ sa soma̍ indra te su̱taḥ piba̍ ||
4yasya̍ mandā̱no andha̍so̱ māgho̍naṁ dadhi̱ṣe śava̍ḥ | a̱yaṁ sa soma̍ indra te su̱taḥ piba̍ ||
translation.text:
2Whose gladdening draught, shed from the points, thou guardest in the midst and end, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!
3In whose wild joy thou settest free the kine held fast within the rock, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!
4This, in whose juice delighting thou gainest the might of Maghavan, This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 450r (numbered 123r by the scribe) (OPenn image 450, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.43.2 ‹yasya tīvra-sutam madam madhyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 450v (numbered 123v by the scribe), begins in RV 6.44.4 ‹-maṃhiṣṭham viśva-carṣaṇim›. Verses 6.43.2-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
2yasya | tīvra-sutam | madam | madhyam antam | ca | rakṣase | ayam | saḥ | somaḥ | indra | te | sutaḥ | piba
3yasya | gāḥ | antaḥ | aśmanaḥ | made | dṛḷhāḥ | ava-asṛjaḥ | ayam | saḥ | somaḥ | indra | te | sutaḥ | piba
4yasya | mandānaḥ | andhasaḥ | māghonam | dadhiṣe | śavaḥ | ayam | saḥ | somaḥ | indra | te | sutaḥ | piba
